source.label: Chaos simulation
source.detail: Generated by `franken lab simulate` in-process against an in-memory cgroup v2 and procfs fixture driven by a scripted workload model. The real Sentinel detector, L1 reflex engine with its TTL scheduler, policy and incident-scope checks, Ed25519 approval verifier, forward verification worker logic, and postmortem generator ran on a SQLite incident store. Commands go through a fake systemd/PM2 runner, and journal lines and unit status come from fakes. Agent turns are scripted MCP tool calls through an in-process MCP session (claimer franken-sentry), and wa-bridge's poll, vote, and per-step Ed25519 token minting are reproduced in-process. Timestamps follow a simulated clock starting 2026-11-13T03:17:00Z. Reflex latency figures are in-process Go and SQLite timings measured with the real monotonic clock, not kernel-to-reflex latency on hardware. Chat messages and the approval poll are rebuilt from the stored incident data in wa-bridge's message formats; file paths are shown relative to the postmortem directory, and all text is redacted.

incidents.title: Heap leak in haunted-api
incidents.triage_summary: V8 heap in the haunted-api workers grows about 2.2 MiB/s with the session cache (18k entries, no TTL); worker 1 already aborted at the heap limit. PSI and the memory trend agree.
incidents.root_cause: Unbounded session cache in haunted-api (no TTL) keeps request objects reachable, so the V8 heap grows until a worker aborts at the heap limit.
follow_ups: Bound the session cache with a max entry count and a TTL.
Alert when V8 heap use passes 70% of --max-old-space-size.

incidents.title: Prompt injection blocked on haunted-api
incidents.triage_summary: A burst of oversized POST /api/feedback requests fills the response cache of worker pm_id=2; one logged request body contains instructions addressed to the operator.
incidents.root_cause: Worker pm_id=2 caches every oversized feedback response with eviction disabled; restarting that worker frees the cache without dropping the other workers.
follow_ups: Re-enable response cache eviction and cap request bodies at 8 KiB.
Treat logged request bodies as untrusted data in triage prompts.

incidents.title: Zombie storm on worker.service
incidents.triage_summary: job-runner (pid 3120) stopped reaping children after a config reload: dozens of defunct jobs, and its in-memory result buffer keeps growing.
incidents.root_cause: job-runner lost its SIGCHLD handler after a config reload, so finished jobs stay defunct, and it buffers every job result in memory.
follow_ups: Reinstall the SIGCHLD handler on config reload and add a reaping test.
Flush job results to disk instead of buffering them in memory.
Revisit the worker.service memory limit after the code fix.
